records.title: Major questions: clear authorization for vast power
records.text: The same day, a vaccination rule for health-care staff stands: it falls within express power to protect patients' health and safety.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Major questions: clear authorization for vast power
records.text: The doctrine is named: in extraordinary cases the agency must point to clear congressional authorization; a merely plausible reading is not enough.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Major questions: clear authorization for vast power
records.text: Power to 'waive or modify' allows modest changes, not mass loan cancellation; Barrett recasts the doctrine as reading text in context.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Protected interests: from privilege to entitlement
records.text: First identify protected liberty or property; then ask what process is due. Roth rejects the privilege label as the test but requires an entitlement source. Loudermill rejects the Arnett plurality’s attempt to let the source statute set the constitutional procedure.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Protected interests: from privilege to entitlement
records.text: Due process protects a legitimate claim of entitlement defined by law or mutual understanding (Roth), whatever the privilege label; once the interest exists, the Constitution, not the statute that created it, sets the minimum process (Loudermill), and unrestricted official discretion can defeat the entitlement.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Protected interests: from privilege to entitlement
records.text: Government employment is a privilege, not property, so dismissal needs no due process; an equally divided Court affirmed in 1951.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Protected interests: from privilege to entitlement
records.text: Officials may not cost a person a private job through a clearance hearing without confrontation unless Congress or the President expressly allows it.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Protected interests: from privilege to entitlement
records.text: No hearing was due to bar a cook from a naval base: the process due depends on the government function and the private interest at stake.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Protected interests: from privilege to entitlement
records.text: Welfare benefits are a statutory entitlement, not a privilege, so ending them triggers due process and a prior hearing.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Protected interests: from privilege to entitlement
records.text: Property means a legitimate claim of entitlement from an independent source such as state law; a one-year appointment gives none.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Protected interests: from privilege to entitlement
records.text: Mutually explicit understandings, not only formal tenure, can create a property interest in continued public employment.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Protected interests: from privilege to entitlement
records.text: A three-Justice plurality says a statute granting a job may also limit its procedures, the 'bitter with the sweet'; six Justices disagree.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Protected interests: from privilege to entitlement
records.text: State law creates the interest, but the Constitution sets the procedure for taking it away; the bitter-with-the-sweet idea is rejected.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Protected interests: from privilege to entitlement
records.text: Meeting eligibility criteria is no entitlement when supply is limited and officials have unrestricted discretion over who gets the benefit.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Protected interests: from privilege to entitlement
records.text: A Colorado court holds that a no-entitlement clause does not defeat a property interest where officials cannot deny funded benefits to the eligible.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: What process is due, and when
records.text: First distinguish general policymaking from a decision about particular persons. Where an individual protected interest is affected, compare timing and safeguards under Mathews. A statutory hearing right can exist independently of constitutional due process.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: What process is due, and when
records.text: Mathews balancing decides what process is due once a protected interest is at stake: a general rule needs no individual hearing (Bi-Metallic), and otherwise notice and a chance to respond scale with the interest, the risk of error and the government's burden; an informal chance to respond followed by a fuller hearing or an ordinary lawsuit often suffices.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: What process is due, and when
records.text: When a body assesses particular owners on individual grounds, each must get notice and a hearing with argument and proof.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: What process is due, and when
records.text: A general rule applied to everyone alike needs no individual hearing; the check on it is political, not procedural.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: What process is due, and when
records.text: Welfare may not be cut off before an evidentiary hearing with oral presentation, confrontation and an impartial decisionmaker.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: What process is due, and when
records.text: Three-factor balancing of private interest, risk of error and government burden; no evidentiary hearing is needed before disability benefits stop.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: What process is due, and when
records.text: School paddling implicates liberty, but common-law limits and later civil and criminal remedies supply the process due; no prior hearing.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: What process is due, and when
records.text: A customer facing a utility shutoff must be told how to dispute the bill and get a chance to present it to someone able to fix it.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: What process is due, and when
records.text: Before firing a tenured employee: notice, an explanation of the evidence and a chance to respond, with a fuller hearing afterward.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: What process is due, and when
records.text: Before an order reinstating a whistleblower, the employer gets the substance of the evidence and a chance to respond, not a trial-type hearing.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: What process is due, and when
records.text: Mathews, modified to weigh the plaintiff's interest, governs private prejudgment attachment; attaching a home without notice or exigency fails.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: What process is due, and when
records.text: After a lawful seizure the owner must be told of it, but not of return remedies set out in published statutes and cases.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: What process is due, and when
records.text: Where an ordinary contract suit can fully protect a disputed claim for payment, that suit is all the process due.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Agency adjudication, public rights and the civil jury
records.text: Article III adjudication and the Seventh Amendment jury right are related but distinct. A new statutory label does not settle either. Jarkesy addresses SEC fraud penalties; it distinguishes Atlas Roofing and does not abolish every administrative adjudication.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Agency adjudication, public rights and the civil jury
records.text: Jarkesy requires an Article III jury for the SEC fraud penalties before it, a legal claim analogous to common-law fraud. It distinguishes Atlas Roofing rather than abolishing agency adjudication. Article III authority, public-rights exceptions and the particular claim and remedy require separate examination.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Agency adjudication, public rights and the civil jury
records.text: Matters of public right, like summary collection of a revenue officer's debt, may be settled by the executive without an Article III trial.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Agency adjudication, public rights and the civil jury
records.text: When the Government enforces new statutory public rights, Congress may assign penalty cases to an agency forum with no jury.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Agency adjudication, public rights and the civil jury
records.text: A government suit for civil penalties is legal in nature, so the defendant gets a jury on liability, though the judge sets the amount.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Agency adjudication, public rights and the civil jury
records.text: Calling a claim a core proceeding cannot strip the jury right; a traditional legal claim against a stranger to the estate is no public right.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Agency adjudication, public rights and the civil jury
records.text: SEC fraud penalties resemble a common-law legal claim and require an Article III jury. The Court distinguishes Atlas Roofing rather than overruling it; public rights and other kinds of agency adjudication remain separate questions.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reasoned decisionmaking: the agency's own reasons and the hard look
records.text: The line concerns whether the agency supplied legally adequate reasons on the relevant record. Chenery limits substitute judicial rationales; State Farm governs rescission; Fox explains policy changes; Ohio v. EPA is an interim assessment on a stay application.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reasoned decisionmaking: the agency's own reasons and the hard look
records.text: The agency must give legally adequate reasons on the record, consider material factors and relevant reliance, and answer significant comments. Chenery ordinarily requires remand rather than substitute judicial policy reasoning; Fox does not impose a heightened standard simply because policy changes. Ohio v. EPA assesses likely error on an interim stay record.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reasoned decisionmaking: the agency's own reasons and the hard look
records.text: A court judges an agency order only on the grounds the agency invoked; it may not supply a policy judgment the agency never made.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reasoned decisionmaking: the agency's own reasons and the hard look
records.text: The concise statement of basis and purpose need not answer every comment but must show the major issues and why the agency chose as it did.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reasoned decisionmaking: the agency's own reasons and the hard look
records.text: Courts ask whether the agency took a 'hard look' and engaged in reasoned decisionmaking; if it did, they defer even if they would differ.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reasoned decisionmaking: the agency's own reasons and the hard look
records.text: Review is searching and careful, on the full administrative record: did the agency weigh the relevant factors, or make a clear error of judgment?
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reasoned decisionmaking: the agency's own reasons and the hard look
records.text: A discretionary requirement fails when the agency does not tie it to the statute's goal or answer concrete objections in the record.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reasoned decisionmaking: the agency's own reasons and the hard look
records.text: An agency may base standards on predicted technology if it answers objections and gives plausible reasons each remaining step can be done in time.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reasoned decisionmaking: the agency's own reasons and the hard look
records.text: The core test: examine the data and connect facts to choice; rescinding a rule gets the same review, and counsel's later reasons do not count.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reasoned decisionmaking: the agency's own reasons and the hard look
records.text: After State Farm's remand, the new passive-restraint rule's present choices survive as reasonably explained; its contingent parts are unripe.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reasoned decisionmaking: the agency's own reasons and the hard look
records.text: A policy change needs no better reasons than the old policy: acknowledge the change, give good reasons, and address reliance and prior findings.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reasoned decisionmaking: the agency's own reasons and the hard look
records.text: The stated reason must be the real one: when the explanation does not match the record, the action goes back to the agency.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reasoned decisionmaking: the agency's own reasons and the hard look
records.text: Rescinding a program requires weighing reliance and alternatives within it; reasons offered later cannot save the original action.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reasoned decisionmaking: the agency's own reasons and the hard look
records.text: A legal error in an agency’s discretionary reasoning ordinarily requires Chenery remand; the court may not simply substitute its own corrected analysis. Narrow remand exceptions are not a general license to supply agency policy.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reasoned decisionmaking: the agency's own reasons and the hard look
records.text: Failing to respond to a significant comment likely makes a rule arbitrary and capricious, and that defect can support a stay.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Substantial-evidence review of agency findings
records.text: This is review of factual support, not independent judicial factfinding. Whole-record review includes evidence against the agency. ADAPSO’s equation of evidentiary support does not erase procedural differences or make every statutory review provision identical.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Substantial-evidence review of agency findings
records.text: An agency finding stands if a reasonable mind could accept the evidence as adequate on the whole record, including evidence that cuts against it; the same quantum of support applies to informal action under arbitrary-and-capricious review, and the bar is not high.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Substantial-evidence review of agency findings
records.text: Substantial evidence is judged on the whole record, including evidence that detracts from the finding and the examiner's contrary report.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Substantial-evidence review of agency findings
records.text: Examining physicians' written reports can be substantial evidence despite hearsay and contrary testimony when the claimant could have subpoenaed them.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Substantial-evidence review of agency findings
records.text: Substantial-evidence and arbitrary-and-capricious review demand the same factual support; the former simply confines it to a formal record.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Substantial-evidence review of agency findings
records.text: A health standard may rest on cumulative, imperfect science, but the agency must show with evidence why a feasible added protection is unneeded.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Substantial-evidence review of agency findings
records.text: An agency must apply the standard it announces; a finding that quietly demands more than that standard lacks substantial evidence.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Substantial-evidence review of agency findings
records.text: The APA's standards govern review of the patent office's fact findings; the stricter clear-error test courts apply to judges does not.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Substantial-evidence review of agency findings
records.text: Informal action needs the same evidentiary support as formal action, drawn from what the agency had before it when it acted.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Substantial-evidence review of agency findings
records.text: The threshold is not high and is applied case by case; an expert's refusal to share underlying data does not automatically defeat it.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reviewing agency inaction and enforcement choices
records.text: Do not treat all inaction alike. Enforcement refusal, denial of a rulemaking petition, rescission of a benefits program and failure to perform a mandatory discrete duty follow distinct review routes.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reviewing agency inaction and enforcement choices
records.text: A refusal to enforce is presumptively unreviewable (Heckler), but denials of rulemaking petitions are reviewable with great deference, rescinding a program that confers benefits is reviewable, and a court can compel only a discrete action the law requires (Norton).
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reviewing agency inaction and enforcement choices
records.text: 'Committed to agency discretion' is a narrow exception for cases with no law to apply; statutory standards make action reviewable.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reviewing agency inaction and enforcement choices
records.text: A decision not to sue to set aside a union election is reviewable, but only for rationality, on the Secretary's statement of reasons.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reviewing agency inaction and enforcement choices
records.text: A refusal to enforce is presumptively unreviewable unless the statute supplies guidelines that limit the agency's enforcement discretion.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reviewing agency inaction and enforcement choices
records.text: A refusal to begin rulemaking is reviewable under a highly deferential standard but still needs a reasoned, record-supported explanation.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reviewing agency inaction and enforcement choices
records.text: A court may compel only a discrete action the agency is legally required to take, not general compliance with a broad mandate.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reviewing agency inaction and enforcement choices
records.text: Denying a rulemaking petition is reviewable, and the agency's reasons must track the statute's criteria, not unrelated policy preferences.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Reviewing agency inaction and enforcement choices
records.text: Ending a program that solicits applications and grants benefits is more than passive nonenforcement, so Heckler's presumption does not bar review.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Rule or order: the agency's choice of procedure
records.text: An agency needs statutory authority for either tool. Chenery II and Bell Aerospace generally leave the choice to the agency; Wyman-Gordon splits over an announced prospective rule while sustaining the specific order. National Petroleum interprets the FTC statute.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Rule or order: the agency's choice of procedure
records.text: Chenery II and Bell Aerospace generally permit a statutorily authorized agency to choose policymaking by adjudication, subject to abuse and unfair retroactivity concerns. Wyman-Gordon has a divided rationale. National Petroleum’s rulemaking holding concerns the FTC statute and later statutory procedures, not an unrestricted power for every agency.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Rule or order: the agency's choice of procedure
records.text: The APA sorts agency action into two kinds, each with its own procedure: rules, which have future effect, and orders, the products of adjudication.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Rule or order: the agency's choice of procedure
records.text: The choice between a general rule and case-by-case adjudication is primarily the agency's; retroactive effect is weighed, not fatal.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Rule or order: the agency's choice of procedure
records.text: No majority: a plurality says a purely prospective rule announced in adjudication evades the APA, but the order against the party is enforced.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Rule or order: the agency's choice of procedure
records.text: The D.C. Circuit reads the FTC Act’s general rulemaking clause to authorize binding rules defining unfair or deceptive practices. The holding concerns that statutory scheme, not every agency’s general rulemaking clause.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Rule or order: the agency's choice of procedure
records.text: The Board may announce new principles through adjudication; the choice is reviewed only for abuse, as where it would upset reliance.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Rulemaking procedure: formal hearings, notice and comment, and the limits on courts
records.text: Informal notice and comment, formal rulemaking and formal adjudication have different triggers. Marathon Oil concerns adjudication, not an exception that makes ordinary rulemaking formal. Vermont Yankee limits added procedures while courts interpret the APA’s existing duties.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Rulemaking procedure: formal hearings, notice and comment, and the limits on courts
records.text: Section 553 is the ordinary notice-and-comment framework, subject to its exemptions and the governing statute. Formal rulemaking has a distinct on-the-record trigger; Marathon Oil concerns formal adjudication. Courts enforce meaningful notice, participation and reasons while Vermont Yankee limits added procedures. Mock addresses a particular proposal at a preliminary stage.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Rulemaking procedure: formal hearings, notice and comment, and the limits on courts
records.text: The APA requires notice, written comment and a statement of basis and purpose; trial-type procedure only when rules must be made on the record.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Rulemaking procedure: formal hearings, notice and comment, and the limits on courts
records.text: In on-the-record rulemaking, parties must be able to test the data behind the agency's summaries, or the findings lack support.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Rulemaking procedure: formal hearings, notice and comment, and the limits on courts
records.text: Formal rulemaking applies only when a statute calls for rules 'on the record after opportunity for an agency hearing' or the like.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Rulemaking procedure: formal hearings, notice and comment, and the limits on courts
records.text: Even short of formal procedure, a rule under substantial-evidence review needs a record whose factual premises parties could test.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Rulemaking procedure: formal hearings, notice and comment, and the limits on courts
records.text: A separate adjudication branch: the Ninth Circuit reads a statutory “public hearing” on disputed facts to trigger formal APA adjudication without “on the record.” This does not expand formal rulemaking under Florida East Coast.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Rulemaking procedure: formal hearings, notice and comment, and the limits on courts
records.text: Notice must disclose the scientific data behind a proposal, and the final statement must answer comments that go to the rule's core.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Rulemaking procedure: formal hearings, notice and comment, and the limits on courts
records.text: Courts may not add procedures to informal rulemaking beyond those the Constitution, the APA and the governing statute require.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Rulemaking procedure: formal hearings, notice and comment, and the limits on courts
records.text: The disclosure rule survives Vermont Yankee: studies the agency relies on must be released for comment; Judge Kavanaugh questions it.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Rulemaking procedure: formal hearings, notice and comment, and the limits on courts
records.text: Vermont Yankee applied: interpretive rules need no notice and comment, even when they change an earlier interpretation.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Rulemaking procedure: formal hearings, notice and comment, and the limits on courts
records.text: Courts may not add an open-mindedness test to notice and comment; the APA's objective requirements, if met, are enough.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Rulemaking procedure: formal hearings, notice and comment, and the limits on courts
records.text: A final rule must be a logical outgrowth of the proposal; the Fifth Circuit held the pistol-brace rule was not, so its challengers were likely to succeed.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Guidance documents: legislative rule, interpretive rule or policy statement
records.text: An interpretation or policy statement differs from a rule with legal force. Older circuit criteria and practical-binding tests must be read in context; Perez abrogates the extra procedure for revising an interpretation rather than authorizing disguised legislative rules.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Guidance documents: legislative rule, interpretive rule or policy statement
records.text: Binding legal effect or creation of new law can make guidance a legislative rule; a genuine interpretation or nonbinding policy statement follows a different route. Perez rejects extra notice-and-comment requirements merely for changing an interpretation. Circuit tests and statutory exceptions still require attention to the specific document.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Guidance documents: legislative rule, interpretive rule or policy statement
records.text: A policy statement only announces what the agency intends; not being a binding norm, it is exempt, but must be defended each time it is applied.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Guidance documents: legislative rule, interpretive rule or policy statement
records.text: A pronouncement with present binding effect that leaves the agency no real discretion is a legislative rule, whatever its label.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Guidance documents: legislative rule, interpretive rule or policy statement
records.text: The D.C. Circuit lists indicia of legislative rules: an independent enforcement basis, CFR publication, express legislative authority or amendment of a legislative rule. Later cases focus on legal effect; publication alone is not a universal conclusive test.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Guidance documents: legislative rule, interpretive rule or policy statement
records.text: A requirement that cannot be derived from a regulation by interpretation, such as a flat eight-foot fence height, is legislative.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Guidance documents: legislative rule, interpretive rule or policy statement
records.text: Guidance explaining a duty within a regulation is interpretive, but a definitive interpretation may not be fundamentally revised without comment.
records.reviewStatus: Reviewed in timeline pass; scope recorded in its audit.

records.title: Guidance documents: legislative rule, interpretive rule or policy statement
records.text: Guidance that states a settled position and binds in practice is reviewable final action and cannot expand a rule without rulemaking.

records.title: Article III standing: injury, traceability, redress
records.text: Article III requires concrete, particularized and actual or imminent injury, traceability and likely redressability.
